headline: One-time gains fuel a blowout quarter, pricing also firms
summary_short: Century Aluminum reported Q1 2026 net sales of $649.2M (+2.4% q/q) and net income of $337.5M (diluted EPS $3.23), boosted by a $287.9M Hawesville sale gain and $33.0M of insurance proceeds. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $231.4M (+35.6% q/q); shipments fell 12.4% q/q on the Iceland Line 2 outage.
summary_long: Net sales rose to $649.2M on higher realized metal prices, even as shipments fell to 122,865 tonnes on the Grundartangi Line 2 outage and lower third-party alumina sales. Net income of $337.5M was inflated by a $287.9M Hawesville gain and $33.0M of insurance proceeds, partly offset by unfavorable power costs from winter weather. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $231.4M (+35.6% q/q) on favorable pricing and mix, offset by power and raw-material cost pressure. Cash rose to $244.1M and liquidity reached $611.0M, aided by $200M of Hawesville proceeds; $74.8M of capex pushed free cash flow negative. Century guided Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA to $315-335M on higher LME/regional premiums and the Mt. Holly expansion.

drivers.explanation: Record net income was driven almost entirely by two one-time items — the Hawesville sale gain and Iceland insurance proceeds — layered on top of a genuinely stronger pricing and EBITDA quarter.
Sequential increase primarily driven by higher realized metal prices, despite lower shipments from the Iceland Line 2 outage and lower third-party alumina sales.

Increase attributable to a one-time $287.9M gain on the Hawesville sale, a $33.0M insurance gain, and favorable LME/regional premium prices, partly offset by unfavorable power and raw-material cost realization.
Gain reflects stronger metal pricing and a favorable product mix, tempered by higher power and raw-material input costs versus the prior quarter.
First full quarter reflecting the Iceland (Grundartangi) Line 2 equipment failure that began in late October 2025 reduced Icelandic output.
Increase driven by $200M of Hawesville sale proceeds and insurance proceeds received, partly offset by $74.8M of capex.

confidence_notes: Company does not disclose a segregated C1 cash cost or AISC-equivalent metric for its aluminum smelting operations; cost detail is limited to COGS and the non-GAAP EBITDA/net-income reconciliations shown above. Net income and operating income for the prior quarter (FY2025 Q4) as returned by our shard's Yahoo-sourced comparators ($1.8M net income matches, but gross profit $82.3M and operating income $33.0M) differ from the $90.6M gross profit / $41.3M operating income shown in this release's own Q4 2025 comparative column — likely a pending SEC-verbatim rederivation gap on the prior-quarter event, not an error in this quarter's figures. Gross profit and operating income were therefore omitted from the KPI table to avoid a misleading q/q delta; free cash flow uses management's operating cash flow less capex (not a company-labeled 'free cash flow' line, which Century does not report). Adjusted net income/EPS and Adjusted EBITDA are company non-GAAP measures reconciled in the release.
